parts.text:
2
Which of the following could have the same units as force?
energy
A
distance
B
energy
time
C
momentum  distance
D
momentum  time

hints: Notice the four expressions combine energy with distance or time, and momentum with distance or time - start by recalling the unit of force, the newton.
Connect energy to work done using $W = F \times d$, then rearrange to see what $\text{energy divided by distance}$ must represent.

Check the other combinations: recall that $\text{energy}/\text{time}$ is power and that momentum is mass times velocity, then test if multiplying or dividing by distance or time can give $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough: Recall force has SI unit newton, $\text{N}$, with base units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ from $F = ma$.
Use the work equation $W = Fd$, where work and energy share the unit joule, $\text{J}$.
Rearrange to $F = W/d$, so dividing an energy in $\text{J}$ by a distance in $\text{m}$ gives $\text{J m}^{-1}$.
Since $1 \text{ J} = 1 \text{ N m}$, then $1 \text{ J m}^{-1} = 1 \text{ N}$, so $\text{energy}/\text{distance}$ matches force.

The other forms do not match: $\text{energy}/\text{time}$ is power in $\text{W}$, while $\text{momentum} \times \text{distance}$ and $\text{momentum} \times \text{time}$ give $\text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-1}$ and $\text{kg m}$ respectively.
Therefore only $\text{energy}/\text{distance}$ could have the same units as force. This is option A.

A.explanation: Work done is $W = Fd$, so $F = W/d$ and $\text{energy}/\text{distance}$ has units of $\text{J m}^{-1} = \text{N}$.

B.explanation: $\text{energy}/\text{time}$ is power with unit $\text{W}$, not force.

C.explanation: Momentum has units $\text{kg m s}^{-1}$, so multiplying by distance gives $\text{kg m}^{2} \text{s}^{-1}$, not $\text{N}$.

D.explanation: Momentum multiplied by time gives $\text{kg m}$, which is not the $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ of force.
